column1: # Assertions whose pass depends on the host's speed. A miss on a runner below
# the reference CPU count is recorded in proof.json's host_speed_failures and
# in the README; it is never a widened local bound (docs/PROOFS.md).
# A UI row excuses exactly one thing, and only on a CI ui-e2e part whose runner
# has fewer CPUs than the row's reference: a failed outcome of the named test
# whose failure is exactly the assertion the row declares. The assertion is
#   lessThan MS                  expect(received).toBeLessThan[OrEqual](expected)
#                                with Expected MS (the bound's own timing miss)
#   visibleWithin MS LOCATOR     expect(locator).toBeVisible() on exactly LOCATOR,
#                                timed out after MS (the page never drew within
#                                the spec's own wait)
# A skip, a missing outcome, any other assertion of the same test (another
# locator's visibility included), and the same miss on a local proof or in the
# release tier (the pre-release gate enforces the budgets on the reference
# class, on any runner) all still fail the proof. A row counts only once the base carries it identically: a
# row a change adds, or a bound it loosens, excuses nothing.
# A Go test row names a package and one top-level test, and excuses exactly one
# wall-clock check of it, and only on a CI integration part whose runner has
# fewer CPUs than the row's reference. Its assertion is
#   timing ID                    the check the test reports under ID through
#                                internal/testsupport/proof (Timing.Check)
# The merger excuses it when it derives all of these from the part itself: the
# ledger shows the test failed, with no crash and no failing subtest, and no
# other test of its job did not pass; the test left its own timing record
# (artifacts/timing/<test>.json) saying it failed nothing but its timing
# checks; the failure output the ledger kept ends in exactly the helper's
# timing-miss lines, one for each missed check of the record; and every missed
# check is declared by a row, is over its bound, carries the bound the row
# declares, and took no longer than the bound scaled by the reference's CPUs
# over the runner's (a runner with a k-th of the reference's CPUs may take k
# times as long, no more; a UI row has no such ceiling). A test that failed with no timing record has no sample to
# excuse and fails the proof, and so does every miss on a local proof. Counts,
# bytes, history shares, deadlock-detector trips and correctness assertions
# never get a row. A Go row whose assertion is "-" is recorded on a miss and
# never excused.
# Columns are TAB-separated: kind, name, member, assertion, bound (seconds),
# reference CPUs, note. kind=ui names a Playwright spec path under ui/ and the
# test's title; kind=test names a Go package and its test.
